Troubleshooting / FAQ

Common problems, and where in the docs to go for the full explanation.

My pipeline isn't processing events

Check the source connector's health field via the Connectors endpoint. A down connector stalls every pipeline that reads from it. If it's healthy, confirm the pipeline itself is active and not paused — see Scheduling & triggers.

Events keep failing and landing in the dead-letter queue

Walk through Error handling & recovery — it covers both diagnosing the failure and replaying events once fixed.

I'm not receiving webhook deliveries

Verify your endpoint returns a 2xx status and that you're checking X-Godzilla-Signature correctly — a rejected signature looks identical to a dropped delivery from the outside. Full details in the Webhooks endpoint reference.

I'm getting 429s

You've hit the standard-tier limit described in Limits, quotas & errors. Back off using the Retry-After header, or review Quotas & billing if your workload needs higher plan tier limits or customized throughput.

Migrating from v1?

A number of "it worked yesterday" reports trace back to v1's offset pagination or polling patterns carried over into v2 code. See the Migration guide.

Still stuck?

Reach the team directly through the appropriate channel:

  • Technical support: support@godzilladocs.dev
  • Sales & Enterprise plans: sales@godzilladocs.dev — see Quotas & billing for plan tiers and custom quota inquiries.
  • Security reports: security@godzilladocs.dev — see Security & compliance overview for our disclosure policy.
Response times

Standard-tier support responds within one business day. Include your workspace ID and, if relevant, a request_id from an error response.

Security & compliance overview

How Godzilla protects data moving through your pipelines.

Encryption

All API traffic requires TLS 1.2+. Connector credentials are encrypted at rest and are never returned in full by any endpoint after creation.

Credential handling

See Authentication for API key handling, and Connectors endpoint for connector credential rotation.

Least privilege

We recommend scoping every source connector's credentials to read-only access, as described in the Connecting a data source guide.

Data residency

Events are processed in the region your workspace was created in and are not replicated across regions by default.

Reporting a vulnerability

Contact the team at security@godzilladocs.dev or via Troubleshooting / FAQ — do not file security reports as public issues.

Quotas & billing v2

Godzilla enforces resource quotas per workspace according to your plan tier. This page details plan limits, quota dimensions, and the exact platform behavior when an account exceeds its quota.

1,000
requests / minute (Standard Tier)

Default API rate limit per workspace. Enterprise plans support customized limits up to 50,000+ req/min.

Plan tiers

Each workspace is subscribed to one of three tiers. Quotas apply across all pipelines, connectors, and API keys created within that workspace.

Plan Tier API Rate Limit Monthly Events Active Pipelines Connectors Support SLA
Developer 100 req/min 50,000 2 3 Community
Standard 1,000 req/min 5,000,000 25 20 1 business day
Enterprise Custom (10,000+) Custom / Unlimited Unlimited Unlimited 24/7 dedicated (1 hr SLA)

Quota dimensions

Godzilla accounts are governed by four primary quota dimensions:

  • API request rate: Per-minute sliding window limits on calls to https://api.godzilladocs.dev/v2. See Limits, quotas & errors for header specifications.
  • Monthly event volume: The total number of events ingested, transformed, and delivered by your pipelines in a monthly billing cycle.
  • Active pipeline concurrency: The maximum number of pipelines running in active state simultaneously. Pipelines in draft or paused state do not count toward this limit.
  • Dead-letter queue retention: How long failed events remain available for inspection and replay (7 days on Developer, 30 days on Standard, 90 days on Enterprise).

What happens when you exceed your quota

Platform behavior depends on which quota dimension is exceeded and your workspace billing settings:

1. API rate limit exceeded

When API request volume exceeds the per-minute threshold, the gateway immediately rejects additional requests with HTTP status 429 Too Many Requests. Responses include a Retry-After header indicating the number of seconds until the rate limit resets.

429-rate-limit-response.json json 
{\n  \"error\": {\n    \"code\": \"rate_limit_exceeded\",\n    \"message\": \"API rate limit of 1000 req/min exceeded. Retry after 12 seconds.\",\n    \"request_id\": \"req_rl_4901b\"\n  }\n}

2. Monthly event quota exceeded

When event processing approaches or passes the monthly quota:

  • Warning notifications: Godzilla issues automated webhook notifications (account.quota_warning at 80% and account.quota_exceeded at 100%) and sends email alerts to workspace admins.
  • Standard tier (auto-overage enabled): Pipelines continue processing without interruption. Overage events are billed at $0.25 per 100,000 events on your monthly invoice.
  • Developer tier & hard caps: If auto-overage is disabled or you are on the Developer tier, pipelines transition to paused state. In-flight events finish processing, while new incoming events are buffered up to connector queue limits before upstream reads pause.
No event drops on overage

Godzilla never silently drops events when an account exceeds its quota. Events either flow with overage pricing or pause safely at the connector stage until the plan is upgraded or the billing cycle rolls over.

3. Pipeline or connector limits exceeded

Attempting to create a pipeline or connector beyond your plan limit via POST /v2/pipelines or POST /v2/connectors returns 403 Forbidden with error code quota_exceeded.

quota-exceeded-response.json json 
{\n  \"error\": {\n    \"code\": \"quota_exceeded\",\n    \"message\": \"Maximum active pipeline limit (25) reached for this workspace. Upgrade your plan to create more pipelines.\",\n    \"request_id\": \"req_lim_9921c\"\n  }\n}

Upgrading and billing management

You can upgrade your plan or configure overage settings at any time:

  • Self-serve upgrades: Upgrade from Developer to Standard instantly in the workspace dashboard under Settings > Billing.
  • Enterprise custom plans: For custom rate limits, VPC peering, and enterprise volume discounts, contact our sales team at sales@godzilladocs.dev or via Troubleshooting / FAQ.
Need help with rate limits or retries?

Read Limits, quotas & errors for HTTP response headers and error codes, or check the Error handling & recovery guide for automated backoff strategies.

  • What happens when you exceed your quota

# Godzilla Docs

> Everything you need to build data pipelines on the Godzilla platform.

## Pages
- [Changelog](https://localhost:3002/changelog): Recent changes to the Godzilla API and platform.
- [Glossary](https://localhost:3002/glossary): Definitions for Godzilla's core terms, each linking to its full explanation.
- [Godzilla Docs](https://localhost:3002/index): Everything you need to build data pipelines on the Godzilla platform.
- [Security & compliance overview](https://localhost:3002/security-and-compliance): How Godzilla handles data in transit and at rest, credential storage, and compliance posture.
- [Troubleshooting / FAQ](https://localhost:3002/troubleshooting): Common problems and fixes across pipelines, connectors, and webhooks.

## api
- [API Reference](https://localhost:3002/api/index): The Godzilla REST API: pipelines (v3), connectors, events, transforms, webhooks, and rate limits.
- [Connectors endpoint](https://localhost:3002/api/connectors): Create, list, and rotate credentials for connectors via the v2 REST API.
- [Events endpoint](https://localhost:3002/api/events): Query and replay events that have flowed through a pipeline via the v2 REST API.
- [Pipelines endpoint](https://localhost:3002/api/pipelines): Create, list, and manage pipelines via the v3 REST API.
- [Pipelines endpoint (v2)](https://localhost:3002/api/pipelines-v2): Legacy documentation for v2 of the Pipelines endpoint.
- [Quotas & billing](https://localhost:3002/api/quotas-billing): Plan tiers, workspace resource limits, overage behavior, and billing policies.
- [Limits, quotas & errors](https://localhost:3002/api/rate-limits-errors): Standard-tier rate limits, pagination envelope, and the v2 API's error response shape.
- [Transforms endpoint](https://localhost:3002/api/transforms): Create and list transform steps within pipelines via the v2 REST API.
- [Webhooks endpoint](https://localhost:3002/api/webhooks): Subscribe to Godzilla platform lifecycle events over outbound HTTP via the v2 REST API.

## concepts
- [Concepts](https://localhost:3002/concepts/index): The core building blocks of Godzilla: pipelines, connectors, events, and schemas.
- [Connectors](https://localhost:3002/concepts/connectors): What a connector is in Godzilla: a pre-built integration to a source or destination system, with its own auth and catalog of built-in types.
- [Events](https://localhost:3002/concepts/events): What an event is in Godzilla: the atomic unit of data moving through a pipeline, plus the platform's own lifecycle events.
- [Pipelines](https://localhost:3002/concepts/pipelines): What a pipeline is in Godzilla: a named, versioned workflow that moves data from a source connector through transform steps to a destination.
- [Schemas](https://localhost:3002/concepts/schemas): How event payload shapes are declared, validated, and evolved in Godzilla.

## getting-started
- [Authentication](https://localhost:3002/getting-started/authentication): Authenticate API requests with a bearer API key.
- [Getting Started](https://localhost:3002/getting-started/index): Everything you need to get up and running with Godzilla data pipelines.
- [Installation](https://localhost:3002/getting-started/installation): Install the Godzilla SDK or start calling the REST API directly.
- [Quickstart](https://localhost:3002/getting-started/quickstart): Go from zero to a running pipeline in five minutes.

## guides
- [Building your first pipeline](https://localhost:3002/guides/building-your-first-pipeline): Create a source connector, a destination connector, and the pipeline that connects them, end to end.
- [Connecting a data source](https://localhost:3002/guides/connecting-a-data-source): Choose the right connector type and authentication method for a new data source.
- [Guides](https://localhost:3002/guides/index): Task-oriented walkthroughs for building, connecting, and operating Godzilla pipelines.
- [Error handling & recovery](https://localhost:3002/guides/handling-errors-and-retries): How Godzilla retries failed events, when they're dead-lettered, and how to replay them.
- [Monitoring & alerts](https://localhost:3002/guides/monitoring-and-alerts): Watch pipeline health and get notified of failures via webhooks before they become incidents.
- [Scheduling & triggers](https://localhost:3002/guides/scheduling-and-triggers): Run a pipeline on a cron schedule or trigger it directly from incoming events.
- [Transforming events in flight](https://localhost:3002/guides/transforming-events-in-flight): Reshape, filter, and enrich events in real time as they move through a pipeline.

## recipes
- [Backfill historical data](https://localhost:3002/recipes/backfill-historical-data): Replay and ingest historical datasets through a pipeline without disrupting real-time event flow.
- [Fan-out to multiple destinations](https://localhost:3002/recipes/fan-out-to-multiple-destinations): Broadcast a single source event stream to multiple independent destinations with isolated error handling.
- [Recipes](https://localhost:3002/recipes/index): Production-tested architecture recipes and patterns for Godzilla data pipelines.

## sdks

Quotas & billing v2

Godzilla enforces resource quotas per workspace according to your plan tier. This page details plan limits, quota dimensions, and the exact platform behavior when an account exceeds its quota.

1,000
requests / minute (Standard Tier)

Default API rate limit per workspace. Enterprise plans support customized limits up to 50,000+ req/min.

Plan tiers

Each workspace is subscribed to one of three tiers. Quotas apply across all pipelines, connectors, and API keys created within that workspace.

Plan Tier API Rate Limit Monthly Events Active Pipelines Connectors Support SLA
Developer 100 req/min 50,000 2 3 Community
Standard 1,000 req/min 5,000,000 25 20 1 business day
Enterprise Custom (10,000+) Custom / Unlimited Unlimited Unlimited 24/7 dedicated (1 hr SLA)

Quota dimensions

Godzilla accounts are governed by four primary quota dimensions:

  • API request rate: Per-minute sliding window limits on calls to https://api.godzilladocs.dev/v2. See Limits, quotas & errors for header specifications.
  • Monthly event volume: The total number of events ingested, transformed, and delivered by your pipelines in a monthly billing cycle.
  • Active pipeline concurrency: The maximum number of pipelines running in active state simultaneously. Pipelines in draft or paused state do not count toward this limit.
  • Dead-letter queue retention: How long failed events remain available for inspection and replay (7 days on Developer, 30 days on Standard, 90 days on Enterprise).

What happens when you exceed your quota

Platform behavior depends on which quota dimension is exceeded and your workspace billing settings:

1. API rate limit exceeded

When API request volume exceeds the per-minute threshold, the gateway immediately rejects additional requests with HTTP status 429 Too Many Requests. Responses include a Retry-After header indicating the number of seconds until the rate limit resets.

429-rate-limit-response.json json 
{
  "error": {
    "code": "rate_limit_exceeded",
    "message": "API rate limit of 1000 req/min exceeded. Retry after 12 seconds.",
    "request_id": "req_rl_4901b"
  }
}

2. Monthly event quota exceeded

When event processing approaches or passes the monthly quota:

  • Warning notifications: Godzilla issues automated webhook notifications (account.quota_warning at 80% and account.quota_exceeded at 100%) and sends email alerts to workspace admins.
  • Standard tier (auto-overage enabled): Pipelines continue processing without interruption. Overage events are billed at $0.25 per 100,000 events on your monthly invoice.
  • Developer tier & hard caps: If auto-overage is disabled or you are on the Developer tier, pipelines transition to paused state. In-flight events finish processing, while new incoming events are buffered up to connector queue limits before upstream reads pause.
No event drops on overage

Godzilla never silently drops events when an account exceeds its quota. Events either flow with overage pricing or pause safely at the connector stage until the plan is upgraded or the billing cycle rolls over.

3. Pipeline or connector limits exceeded

Attempting to create a pipeline or connector beyond your plan limit via POST /v2/pipelines or POST /v2/connectors returns 403 Forbidden with error code quota_exceeded.

quota-exceeded-response.json json 
{
  "error": {
    "code": "quota_exceeded",
    "message": "Maximum active pipeline limit (25) reached for this workspace. Upgrade your plan to create more pipelines.",
    "request_id": "req_lim_9921c"
  }
}

Upgrading and billing management

You can upgrade your plan or configure overage settings at any time:

  • Self-serve upgrades: Upgrade from Developer to Standard instantly in the workspace dashboard under Settings > Billing.
  • Enterprise custom plans: For custom rate limits, VPC peering, and enterprise volume discounts, contact our sales team at sales@godzilladocs.dev or via Troubleshooting / FAQ.
Need help with rate limits or retries?

Read Limits, quotas & errors for HTTP response headers and error codes, or check the Error handling & recovery guide for automated backoff strategies.

  • What happens when you exceed your quota
